name: mc-output-accuracy
description: Monte Carlo local-mismatch spread of the closed-loop LDO output voltage against the ratified 1.8 V +/-2% window: per-corner mean (the deterministic terms) and sigma (the statistical term), 1000 samples at each of the 81 mandated PVT points.
claim: README output-accuracy row -- 1.8 V +/-2% (+/-36 mV, 3 sigma), regulator-only per README note 2. This record substantiates the STATISTICAL half of design/error_amp.md S3's offset budget (the amp input-pair + mirror mismatch term, target 3 sigma <= 2.33 mV input-referred / 3.49 mV output-referred) together with the deterministic mean it sits on. The feedback-divider mismatch term is NOT simulable against this PDK (mis_r = 0, sim/devchar/CONCLUSIONS.md S2) and enters as S3.2's fixed 3.36 mV assumption; load regulation is a separate 18 mV allowance verified by #12. The full combine against the window is sim/mc-output-accuracy/README.md.

operating_conditions.load_current: 1 mA, set by a 1.8 kOhm load resistor per DUT copy -- the light-load point README note 1 makes binding for the accuracy-class rows. See the testbench header for why a resistor and not an ideal current sink (a sink leaves the DC solve unbounded and a fraction of the Monte Carlo samples do not converge).
operating_conditions.output_cap: 1.0 uF, ESR = 100 mOhm (the DR-0001 nominal), one network per DUT copy. Present so this deck's DUT environment matches the other ldo_core benches; it does not affect a DC operating point.
operating_conditions.enable_state: enabled (EN = VIN), steady state -- ldo_core's Men clamp off, pass device under loop control
operating_conditions.reference: ideal 1.2 V source inside ldo_core (design/ldo_core.sch's Vref1). The reference's own error is EXCLUDED from this claim per README note 2 (regulator-only window); the bandgap companion block's tolerance is not this repo's budget line and is not added to this deck's combine.
operating_conditions.statistical_switches: sw_stat_mismatch = 1, sw_stat_global = 0 -- intra-die local mismatch only, redrawn per sample by mc_source. Global spread is off because sim/devchar/CONCLUSIONS.md S2 measured it to be exactly common-mode across a matched pair, so it moves neither the divider ratio nor the amplifier offset.
operating_conditions.what_is_not_monte_carlod: The feedback divider. ldo_core draws it as ideal SPICE resistors, and even the PDK subcircuits hard-code mis_r = 0, so a divider Monte Carlo returns sigma = 0 by construction. design/error_amp.md S3.2's fixed 3.36 mV (3 sigma) assumption is RSS'd on afterwards in sim/mc-output-accuracy/README.md. The divider_exact_uv measurement below is the in-situ proof that the divider contributed nothing to this run's sigma.

n_samples.description: sample-count integrity: every corner must have completed the full 25 x 40 Monte Carlo loop, or its sigma is not the sigma this record's Statistical convention field claims

n_bad_solves.description: count of solves in which any DUT copy landed further than 100 mV from 1.8 V, i.e. a DC solve that did not find a regulating operating point. ngspice reports a failed gmin/source-stepping solve only as a warning and still hands back its last iterate, so an unconverged sample would otherwise enter the distribution as a plausible-looking outlier and inflate sigma. Zero tolerated: a nonzero count invalidates the run's statistics rather than merely widening them.

sigma_mv.description: INTEGRITY FLOOR, not a spec line. The failure mode this whole experiment exists to prevent is a silently-disabled mismatch model returning sigma = 0 -- which is exactly what this PDK's resistor cards do (sim/devchar/CONCLUSIONS.md S2). A DC operating point is deterministic, so with the statistical switches off every sample would be bit-identical and sigma would be exactly zero. The PDK's design.ngspice defaults sw_stat_mismatch = 0 and is included after the harness's .param block, so the testbench re-asserts the switch; if that re-assertion ever stops working this check FAILS loudly instead of reporting a flawless distribution.

sigma3_mv.description: design/error_amp.md S3's output-referred target for the amp input-pair + mirror mismatch term (3 sigma, referred through 1/beta = 1.5). S3.1 asks #13 to VERIFY this number, not merely report it.

vos_in_sigma3_mv.description: the same target read at the amplifier's own inputs: design/error_amp.md S3.1's Pelgrom-derived 3 sigma <= 2.33 mV input-referred. This is sigma3_mv referred back through the divider ratio, which divider_exact_uv verifies is exactly 1.5 sample by sample.

worst_abs_mv.description: no single Monte Carlo sample may exceed the 18 mV one-sided STATIC budget of design/error_amp.md S3 (the +/-36 mV window less the 18 mV load-regulation allowance). This is a per-sample worst case over 1000 samples, so it is a strictly stronger statement than the 3 sigma claim.

divider_exact_uv.description: max over all samples of |dVOUT - 1.5*dFB| in uV. The feedback divider sits between those two nodes, so any mismatch in it breaks the identity. Pinning the residual under 1 uV is the in-situ evidence that this run's sigma is the amplifier's alone -- which is what makes design/error_amp.md S3.2's separately hand-budgeted divider term additive rather than double-counted, and what would catch a future netlist that starts Monte-Carloing the divider and silently reports sigma = 0 for it.

mean_mv.description: design/error_amp.md S3's DETERMINISTIC sum (systematic offset 0.91 mV + line regulation 1.65 mV, both output-referred and added linearly). The per-corner Monte Carlo mean is where those two terms land; sigma is where the statistical term lands. Keeping them in separate columns is what stops the two budget classes being conflated.
